parts.visual:
A startup builds an incredible photo-sharing app. It is growing fast, but running out of server money. Suddenly, the CEO of Facebook calls. Facebook offers $1 Billion in cash to buy the startup entirely. The founder signs the paper. The startup no longer exists as an independent entity; it is now just a department inside Facebook.

The Acquisition:
1. M&A: Mergers and Acquisitions. 90% of successful tech startups do not IPO; they are simply bought by a massive tech giant (Google, Apple, Microsoft) who wants their technology or their users.
2. The Strategic Premium: A giant won't just pay what your revenue is worth. They will pay a massive 'premium' (extra money) because your startup either perfectly completes their product line, or is so dangerous that they must buy you to kill you.
parts.audio: Startups are bought, not sold. If you desperately run around trying to sell your company, nobody will buy it. If you build a company so terrifyingly fast that Google is afraid of you, Google will show up with a checkbook to neutralize the threat.

questions.question: What is 'Due Diligence' during an acquisition?
options: The audit of terror. Before a Giant hands over $500 Million, their army of lawyers and accountants spend 3 months secretly ripping apart your startup. They look at every line of code, every employment contract, and every tax return to ensure you aren't lying.
questions.correct_answer: The audit of terror. Before a Giant hands over $500 Million, their army of lawyers and accountants spend 3 months secretly ripping apart your startup. They look at every line of code, every employment contract, and every tax return to ensure you aren't lying.
questions.explanation: Skeletons in the closet will kill the deal.

questions.question: Listen to the founder explaining 'Earn-Outs'. Why did the founder hate working at Google after selling their startup?
questions.tts_text: Google bought us for $50 million, but I didn't get the money on day one. They structured it as an 'Earn-Out'. I only get the money if I stay an obedient Google employee for three years and hit their corporate revenue goals. I felt like a hostage.
options: The Golden Handcuffs. Giants use earn-outs to prevent the brilliant founders from taking the cash and immediately quitting to start a new company. The founders are forced to endure years of corporate bureaucracy to unlock their full payout.
questions.correct_answer: The Golden Handcuffs. The Giants use earn-outs to prevent the brilliant founders from taking the cash and immediately quitting to start a new company. The founders are forced to endure years of corporate bureaucracy to unlock their full payout.
questions.explanation: You get rich, but you lose your freedom.

questions.question: Why did Facebook famously buy Instagram for $1 Billion when Instagram had 13 employees and zero revenue?
options: Defensive Acquisition. Facebook saw that users were shifting from desktop text to mobile photos. Instagram was a direct existential threat. Facebook didn't buy a revenue stream; they paid $1 Billion to eliminate the only company that could kill them.
questions.correct_answer: Defensive Acquisition. Facebook saw that users were shifting from desktop text to mobile photos. Instagram was a direct existential threat. Facebook didn't buy a revenue stream; they paid $1 Billion to eliminate the only company that could kill them.
questions.explanation: Fear is the most expensive emotion in Silicon Valley.

questions.question: What happens if a startup is bought in an 'All-Stock Deal' (e.g., paid in Microsoft stock instead of cash), and Microsoft's stock crashes the next day?
options: The founders lose their wealth. Accepting stock instead of cash is a massive gamble. You are tying your ultimate exit value to the future performance of the acquiring Giant. If the Giant fails, your exit fails, even after the papers are signed.
questions.correct_answer: The founders lose their wealth. Accepting stock instead of cash is a massive gamble. You are tying your ultimate exit value to the future performance of the acquiring Giant. If the Giant fails, your exit fails, even after the papers are signed.
questions.explanation: Stock is just paper until it is sold.

questions.question: Order the words to describe the reality of acquisitions:
questions.explanation: If you have to beg someone to buy you, you have no leverage.
